extracted.intended_audience: SEC reporting professionals, public company accountants and legal advisers at registrants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and reviewing disclosures of non-GAAP financial measures to ensure compliance with Regulation G and SEC Regulation S-K Item 10(e), for use in SEC filings, press releases, investor presentations, and other public communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Regulation G
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation G applies to all public releases or disclosure of non-GAAP measures, even if such information is not part of a registrant’s SEC filing (e.g., conference calls, investor presentations, and webcasts) and regardless of whether the information is furnished to or filed with the SEC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation G applies whenever a registrant, or person acting on its behalf, publicly discloses or releases material information that includes a non-GAAP financial measure. Such information may be furnished to or filed with the SEC or publicly disclosed or released in another manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-GAAP measures must not be misleading (Regulation G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-GAAP financial measures must not be misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing potentially misleading non-GAAP measures, registrants should consider factors discussed in later sections (see Section 4.3). Avoid presentation or adjustments that obscure GAAP results or create an inaccurate impression of financial performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of the most directly comparable GAAP measure (Regulation G)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most directly comparable GAAP measure must be presented alongside the non-GAAP measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The GAAP measure should be presented in a way that makes the relationship between the non‑GAAP and GAAP measure clear; the summary table in the roadmap indicates this presentation is required for all non‑GAAP disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative reconciliation to the most directly comparable GAAP measure (Regulation G)
rubrics_metrics.description: A quantitative reconciliation of the non-GAAP financial measure to the most comparable GAAP measure must be presented for (1) a historical non-GAAP measure and (2) forward-looking information (to the extent available without unreasonable effort).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numeric reconciliation showing how the non‑GAAP measure is derived from the GAAP measure. For forward-looking non‑GAAP measures, include reconciliation to the extent the information is available without unreasonable effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Item 10(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 10(e) applies to all SEC filings, such as registration statements, proxy statements, and Forms 10-K and 10-Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 10(e) expands on Regulation G and imposes additional filing-specific requirements; registrants should apply these rules whenever non‑GAAP measures appear in SEC filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominence of the comparable GAAP measure (Item 10(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: That the prominence of the most directly comparable GAAP measure presented be equal to or greater than that of the non-GAAP measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In SEC filings (and in press releases furnished on Form 8‑K), ensure the GAAP measure is displayed with prominence equal to or greater than the non‑GAAP measure (formatting, placement, labeling, etc., should reflect this prominence requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of reasons why non-GAAP is useful (Item 10(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement indicating the reasons why the registrant believes that the non-GAAP measure provides useful information to investors about the registrant’s financial condition and results of operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a narrative explaining management’s rationale for using the non‑GAAP measure and how it provides useful perspective to investors—this is required in filings and certain furnished releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of additional management uses (Item 10(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent material, a statement disclosing the additional purposes, if any, for which the registrant uses the non-GAAP measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If management uses the non‑GAAP measure for other material purposes (e.g., internal performance metrics, compensation), disclose those additional uses where material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press releases furnished on Form 8‑K follow Item 10(e) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure requirements for press releases furnished on Form 8-K are the same as those in Item 10(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 8‑K, Item 2.02 requires registrants to furnish releases announcing material nonpublic financial information about completed annual or quarterly periods; Item 2.02 specifies that the requirements in Item 10(e)(1)(i) apply to such disclosures. If a registrant elects to file the release, all Item 10(e) requirements apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple presentations of the same non-GAAP measure
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC’s rules do not address situations where the same non-GAAP measure is presented in multiple sections of a filing; a registrant may repeat the disclosure each time the measure is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because repetitive disclosures may not be beneficial, an alternative is to provide the Item 10(e) disclosures for all non‑GAAP measures in one section of the filing and cross‑reference that section each time the measure is presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation in glossy annual reports and incorporation consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-GAAP measures included in a furnished glossy annual report are generally subject only to Regulation G; however, if the glossy annual report is incorporated by reference in a filed report, Item 10(e) requirements and prohibitions apply as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC amended Rule 101 to require glossy annual reports submitted electronically on EDGAR in PDF to be treated as furnished; registrants should consult legal advisers about whether a glossy report may be considered filed (e.g., via incorporation by reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where Regulation G and Item 10(e) do not apply
rubrics_metrics.description: In certain situations, Regulation G and Item 10(e) do not apply. For example, they do not apply to non-GAAP measures related to projections or forecasts provided to a financial adviser as part of a proposed business combination, or measures required to be disclosed by a governmental authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section 2.3 for discussion of measures that do not meet the definition of a non‑GAAP measure under the Rules; consult guidance and C&DIs for specific exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary table of required disclosures by context
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise summary (table) showing which disclosure elements are required under Regulation G, Item 10(e) in SEC filings, and press releases furnished to the SEC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table indicates: presentation of the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure is required for all disclosure types; presentation with equal or greater prominence is required for SEC filings and furnished press releases; quantitative reconciliation is required across contexts (historical and forward‑looking as applicable); statements of usefulness and additional management uses are required in filings and furnished releases (as marked). Use the table to determine which specific elements to include based on disclosure context.
